editorial:
Imagine being the personal assistant to the world's most famous vampire for centuries. That is exactly the nightmare Renfield is living. You get to see a side of Dracula we have never seen before: a moody, controlling boss who treats his helper like garbage. The vibe is a wild mix of a workplace comedy and a bloody horror flick. You will love how Renfield just wants to quit his job and start over, especially when he meets a tough police officer who actually understands what it is like to deal with a toxic person. It is a fresh, funny take on the old vampire myth that does not take itself too seriously.

Nicholas Hoult is great as the stressed-out servant, but Nicolas Cage steals every scene he is in by being completely over the top. The action is gory and fast, which keeps you from getting bored. While the plot is pretty simple, the jokes land well.
endingExplained: In the big finale, Renfield finally stands up to Dracula and breaks the magical bond between them. With the help of Rebecca, he fights back against the vampire lord. After a messy battle involving a lot of blood and chaos, Dracula is finally defeated and killed for good. Renfield is finally free from his master and gets to live a normal life, finding peace and a real friendship with Rebecca.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark humor and monsters
